newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian regulator approves Eni/Enel joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Italian regulator approves Eni/Enel joint venture.

text.p: The Italian anti-trust regulator said on Friday it had approved a planned electricity production joint venture between energy giant Eni and utility Enel, provided Enel later sold its stake in the operation.
State-controlled Eni and Enel announced earlier this year that they wanted to set up the country's largest independent electricity production company.
Enel pledged eventually to place some or all of its holding in the venture on the market.

Italy's independent electricity producers, led by Edison, complained that the new outfit could create a barrier to the entry of other producers into the market and obstruct the liberalisaton of the state-dominated electricity sector.
But Italy's anti-trust watchdog gave its blessing to the plan, with the proviso that Enel soon sells out.

"The new company will only aid the process towards the liberalisation of the electricity market if Enel gives up its stake, in a defined manner and in a reasonably fast time period," the anti-trust regulator said in a statement.
Enel and Eni said they planned to float a stake in their new electricity production joint venture, but had not yet decided how much.
The regulator added in its statement that to encourage competition in the Italian electricity sector, Enel needed to give up control of a number of its power plants.
